_comment: Ready to paste into any MCP client. Replace /absolute/path/to/salesforce-mcp
with wherever you put the folder, then keep ONE of the two salesforce entries
Most clients read the `mcpServers` key below. Two do not, and they want the
same contents under a different name -- see the two `_alternate_key_*` blocks
at the bottom. Nothing about the server changes; only where the host looks.

env.SF_CLIENT_ID: <Consumer Key of the External Client App>

_notes: The private key goes on ONE line with \n between its PEM lines. JSON has no
multi-line strings, and the connector restores the newlines on the way in.
Credentials are passed here rather than left in .env because a client starts
the server from its own working directory, where .env is usually out of
reach. An environment variable always wins over the file, so there is no
ambiguity if both exist. If your client lets you set a working directory,
pointing it at the project folder works too.
SF_LOGIN_URL defaults to the sandbox host. A Developer Edition org
authenticates at https://login.salesforce.com and additionally needs
SF_ALLOW_PRODUCTION=true -- deliberately explicit, so a typo cannot send
writes to a real production org.
The Docker variant needs -i to keep stdin open; that is how the client
talks to it. Build the image once with `docker build -t salesforce-connector .`
